description: Deploy and run apps, workers, jobs, Postgres, and Valkey on Ownkube from your coding agent. Read logs and metrics, roll back a release, set variables and spend limits. Hosted, with OAuth sign-in.
name: Ownkube
author: Ownkube

prompts.name: deploy_repo
prompts.title: Deploy a repo on Ownkube
prompts.description: Step-by-step plan for deploying a code repository on Ownkube Compute: check the fit, sign in, connect GitHub, fund the wallet, get the human's approval, deploy and verify.

arguments.name: repo
arguments.description: GitHub repository as owner/name. Omit for the repo in the current workspace.

arguments.name: region
arguments.description: Region id from list_regions. Omit to pick the one closest to the users.

resources.name: ownkube-runbook
resources.title: Agent runbook
resources.description: Official instructions for a coding agent deploying a repo on Ownkube: connecting this server, the okctl CLI, the wallet, deploying, databases and caches, and verifying.

resources.name: ownkube-docs-index
resources.title: Docs index
resources.description: Index of the Ownkube site and docs with a link and one-line summary for each page. Read it to find the page for a feature before guessing.

tools.name: connect_aws_account
tools.title: Connect AWS account
tools.description: Start connecting an AWS account. Returns CloudFormation artifacts: a `quickCreateUrl` for a human to click Create, and a `template` block to deploy the stack yourself with existing AWS credentials. Poll get_aws_account until status is `verified` or `failed`. Confirm with the user before calling.

tools.name: list_aws_accounts
tools.title: List AWS accounts
tools.description: Inventory every AWS (cloud) account connected to the organization, with each one's verification status. Call this before create_cluster: it returns the cloudAccountId that create_cluster requires. Second step of the discovery spine after list_organizations.

tools.name: get_aws_account
tools.title: Get AWS account
tools.description: Fetch one connected AWS account's onboarding and verification status by its Ownkube account id (from list_aws_accounts).

accountId.description: The Ownkube AWS account row id.

tools.name: verify_aws_account
tools.title: Verify AWS account
tools.description: Force-verify a connecting AWS account. Normally the stack's phone-home finalizes it automatically; pass `awsAccountId` to assume the role directly before the callback arrives.

accountId.description: The Ownkube AWS account row id.

awsAccountId.description: 12-digit AWS account ID. Supply it to verify immediately (autonomous mode) instead of waiting for the stack's phone-home.

tools.name: reconnect_aws_account
tools.title: Reconnect AWS account
tools.description: Re-arm an account whose access stack was removed. Re-arms the existing account in place and returns a fresh CloudFormation link; re-running the stack recreates the role and re-verifies the same account.

accountId.description: The Ownkube AWS account row id.

tools.name: resync_aws_account
tools.title: Resync AWS account
tools.description: Re-run account setup on a verified account. Re-applies the shared roles and policies; safe to call to pick up an available upgrade (`needsUpgrade: true`).

accountId.description: The Ownkube AWS account row id.

tools.name: remove_aws_account
tools.title: Remove AWS account
tools.description: Remove a connected AWS account. Blocked while any cluster still references it (the cross-account role is required to tear infrastructure down), so destroy those clusters first. Confirm with the user before calling.

accountId.description: The Ownkube AWS account row id.

tools.name: list_clusters
tools.title: List clusters
tools.description: Inventory all clusters in the organization. Start here for cluster work: it returns the clusterId required by get_cluster, get_cluster_status, list_deployments, and destroy_cluster, plus each cluster's cloudAccountId. Third step of the discovery spine after list_aws_accounts.

tools.name: get_cluster
tools.title: Get cluster
tools.description: Fetch one cluster's full configuration and state by clusterId (from list_clusters), including its cloudAccountId and platform/infrastructure versions.

tools.name: get_cluster_status
tools.title: Get cluster status
tools.description: Poll one cluster's live status and provisioning progress by clusterId. Use after create_cluster (which returns the clusterId) until status reports `active` or `failed`.

tools.name: create_cluster
tools.title: Create cluster
tools.description: Provision a new Starter cluster (the self-hosted shape) into a verified AWS account (`cloudAccountId` from list_aws_accounts). Returns immediately with a `clusterId` and `creating` status; poll get_cluster_status until it reports `active` or `failed`. Confirm with the user before calling. Production (`clusterType: eks`) is not self-serve — tell the user to contact us to enable a Production cluster.

cluster.description: The cluster configuration (name, clusterType, cloudAccountId, region, ...).

tools.name: destroy_cluster
tools.title: Destroy cluster
tools.description: Tear a cluster down by id. This is irreversible. Blocked when the cluster still has active deployments unless `force` is true. Confirm with the user before calling.

force.description: Destroy even when the cluster still has active deployments (default false).

tools.name: cancel_cluster_creation
tools.title: Cancel cluster creation
tools.description: Cancel an in-flight cluster creation by id. Valid only while the cluster is still `creating`.

tools.name: list_boxes
tools.title: List Compute box sizes
tools.description: List Ownkube Compute box sizes and monthly prices: `database` and `cache` boxes (required: a database or cache on Ownkube Compute must be created with `billingMode: "reserved"` and `skuId` set to one of these ids) and optional reserved `web` boxes for web/worker (metered is the default). Boxes can be upgraded with update_deployment but not downsized.

tools.name: list_regions
tools.title: List Compute regions
tools.description: List the regions available for deploying on Ownkube Compute (the managed, no-cluster path). Call this before create_deployment on that path: pass a returned region `id` as the deployment's `region` while omitting `clusterId`. An empty list (or `available: false`) means the Compute path is off.

tools.name: list_marketplace_apps
tools.title: List marketplace apps
tools.description: List the marketplace: ready-made open-source apps (for example n8n or Directus) that deploy in one call with their database and cache wired in. Use a returned `slug` with get_marketplace_app and deploy_marketplace_app.

tools.name: get_marketplace_app
tools.title: Get marketplace app
tools.description: Fetch one marketplace app by slug: what it creates, the variables set for you, and the `inputs` to collect from the user before deploy_marketplace_app.

tools.name: check_marketplace_app
tools.title: Check marketplace deploy
tools.description: Dry-run a marketplace deploy: validate the inputs and name prefix without creating anything. Call before deploy_marketplace_app and fix every returned error.

inputs.description: Values for the app's declared inputs (see get_marketplace_app), keyed by input `key`.

baseName.description: Name prefix for every piece (`<baseName>-<ref>`). Defaults to the app id. Lowercase letters, digits, dashes.

tools.name: deploy_marketplace_app
tools.title: Deploy marketplace app
tools.description: Deploy a marketplace app with its database and cache in one call. For Ownkube Compute pass `region` (from list_regions) and no clusterId; if the app includes a database or cache, also pass `dbSkuId` / `cacheSkuId` from list_boxes. For your own cluster pass `clusterId`. Collect the app's `inputs` first (get_marketplace_app) and run check_marketplace_app. Follow progress with get_deployment_status on the returned deployment ids.

region.description: Ownkube Compute region id (from list_regions). Set this or `clusterId`, not both.

clusterId.description: Your own active cluster to deploy into. Set this or `region`, not both.

projectId.description: Owning project. Defaults to the organization's Default.

environmentId.description: Environment to deploy into; must belong to `projectId`. Defaults to the project's default environment.

inputs.description: Values for the app's declared inputs (see get_marketplace_app), keyed by input `key`.

dbSkuId.description: Database box id (from list_boxes `database`). Required on Ownkube Compute when the app includes a database.

cacheSkuId.description: Cache box id (from list_boxes `cache`). Required on Ownkube Compute when the app includes a cache.

baseName.description: Name prefix for every piece (`<baseName>-<ref>`). Defaults to the app id. Lowercase letters, digits, dashes.

tools.name: delete_marketplace_app
tools.title: Delete marketplace app
tools.description: Delete a deployed marketplace app as one unit: the app and its database and cache, including their data. Confirm with the user before calling.

templateInstanceId.description: From the deploy result, or `templateInstanceId` on any of the app's deployments.

tools.name: get_wallet
tools.title: Get the prepaid wallet balance
tools.description: Read the organization's live prepaid wallet balance (granted, consumed, remaining) plus how much credit was loaded by inflow reason. Check this before deploying on Ownkube Compute — a deploy needs a positive balance.

tools.name: get_spend_controls
tools.title: Get spend controls
tools.description: Read the organization's optional monthly budget cap, what happens at the cap (notify vs pause), and the spend-alert thresholds.

tools.name: set_spend_controls
tools.title: Set spend controls
tools.description: Create or update the monthly budget cap and spend alerts. Set budgetAction 'pause' to actually cap the bill (suspends compute, data retained, at the cap); 'notify' only alerts. Only the fields you pass are changed. Confirm with the user before calling.

monthlyBudgetUsd.description: Monthly spend cap in USD, or null to clear it.

budgetAction.description: At the cap: 'notify' alerts only; 'pause' suspends compute.

alertsEnabled.description: Turn spend alerts at the thresholds on or off.

alertThresholdsPct.description: Percent-of-budget thresholds that fire a spend alert.

tools.name: get_credit_status
tools.title: Get account credit status
tools.description: Read the organization's prepaid wallet: whether Ownkube Compute is available, the live balance, and the wallet top-up minimum. Check this before deploying on Ownkube Compute — a deploy needs a positive balance.

tools.name: redeem_promo_code
tools.title: Redeem a promo code
tools.description: Add a promo campaign's credit to the organization's wallet. Each organization and each user can redeem a campaign once. Claiming needs a card on file, which the user adds in the Ownkube dashboard (it is never charged); you never handle card details. Some campaigns' credit expires: expiresAt says when any unspent part lapses. A refusal is not an error: the result has ok false, a reason (not_found, full, ended, not_started, claimed, existing_account, unverified_email, other_offer, card_required, card_used), and a message to show the user.

code.description: The promo code, e.g. from a `/login?ref=<code>` link.

tools.name: open_customer_portal
tools.title: Open the billing customer portal
tools.description: Create a customer-portal session and return a browser URL to manage payment method, invoices, and subscription. Hand the URL to the user. An error with code PRECONDITION_FAILED means the org has no billing account yet (start a plan first).

tools.name: start_subscription_checkout
tools.title: Start a plan subscription checkout
tools.description: Create a checkout for a monthly plan — `personal` ($5/mo) or `team` ($20/mo) — each of which loads that much wallet credit every cycle. Returns a browser URL; hand it to the user to complete payment. The subscription activates once the payment settles.

tier.description: The plan to subscribe to: `personal` ($5/mo) or `team` ($20/mo). Each loads that much wallet credit every cycle.

tools.name: top_up_wallet
tools.title: Top up the prepaid wallet
tools.description: Create a checkout to add a custom amount of credit (USD) to the organization's prepaid wallet. Use get_credit_status to read the minimum (topUpMinUsd) and the plan's cap (topUpMaxUsd) first — an amount below the minimum returns BAD_REQUEST, one above the cap returns PRECONDITION_FAILED with the plan upgrade that lifts it. Returns a browser URL; hand it to the user to complete payment. The balance updates once the payment settles.

amountUsd.description: Amount to add to the wallet, in USD. Must be at least the top-up minimum (see `topUpMinUsd` on GET /v1/credit).

tools.name: get_current_usage
tools.title: Get the live burn rate
tools.description: Read the current metered vCPU + memory in use and the resulting hourly cost across everything the organization runs.

tools.name: get_month_to_date_usage
tools.title: Get month-to-date usage and cost
tools.description: Read usage totals (vCPU-hours, memory-GiB-hours, egress) and the gross cost drawn from the wallet so far this calendar month.

tools.name: get_projected_month_cost
tools.title: Get the projected month cost
tools.description: Read a naive straight-line projection of the month's wallet draw (month-to-date cost scaled to the full month). Volatile early in the month.

tools.name: get_usage_history
tools.title: Get the daily usage series
tools.description: Read per-day usage and cost for the current calendar month, zero-filled for a continuous series.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.title: List projects
tools.description: List the organization's projects and return the projectId that create_environment and create_deployment take. A Default project is auto-seeded, so this always returns at least one.

tools.name: get_project
tools.title: Get project
tools.description: Fetch one project (name, slug, color, description) by projectId (from list_projects).

tools.name: create_project
tools.title: Create project
tools.description: Create a new project — a top-level workspace grouping for environments and apps.

slug.description: Lowercase, starts with a letter; letters, numbers, hyphens only.

tools.name: update_project
tools.title: Update project
tools.description: Update a project's name, color, or description by id.

tools.name: delete_project
tools.title: Delete project
tools.description: Delete a project by id. The Default project can't be deleted, and a project with live environments or deployments is blocked until they're removed. Confirm with the user before calling.

tools.name: list_environments
tools.title: List environments
tools.description: List the organization's environments and return the environmentId that list_deployments and create_deployment take. Default Development and Production environments are auto-seeded, so this always returns at least two.

tools.name: get_environment
tools.title: Get environment
tools.description: Fetch one environment (name, color, shared env vars) by environmentId (from list_environments).

tools.name: create_environment
tools.title: Create environment
tools.description: Create a new environment in a project. Omit projectId to use the organization's default project.

projectId.description: Owning project. Omit to use the organization's default project.

slug.description: Lowercase, starts with a letter; letters, numbers, hyphens only.

tools.name: update_environment
tools.title: Update environment
tools.description: Update an environment's name, color, or description by id.

tools.name: replace_environment_env
tools.title: Replace environment env vars
tools.description: Replace an environment's ENTIRE shared env-var set (a full overwrite, not a patch: any variable you omit is deleted) and redeploy every cluster-bound app that inherits them so the change takes effect immediately. To edit one variable, first read the current set with get_environment and send it back with your change applied. Confirm with the user before calling.

secret.description: Mark as secret so the value is never returned on reads. Echo a saved secret back with an empty `value` to keep the previous value.

value.description: The variable value. For secrets: reads blank secret values, so a secret you read back arrives with an empty value. Sending that empty value here KEEPS the previously saved secret (empty is the passthrough sentinel) rather than clearing it. To genuinely clear a secret, drop the variable from the set entirely; to change it, send the new plaintext.

env.description: The full shared env-var set for the environment (replaces the existing set). Every cluster-bound app in the environment is redeployed to apply it.

tools.name: delete_environment
tools.title: Delete environment
tools.description: Delete an environment by id. Blocked while any deployments still reference it. Confirm with the user before calling.

tools.name: list_registries
tools.title: List container registries
tools.description: List the container registries connected to your organization. Returns the registryId that create_deployment accepts to pull private images.

tools.name: get_registry
tools.title: Get container registry
tools.description: Get a single container registry connection by registryId (from list_registries).

tools.name: list_deployments
tools.title: List deployments
tools.description: List deployments. Provide clusterId (from list_clusters) to scope to one cluster, environmentId (from list_environments) to scope to one environment, projectId (from list_projects) to scope to one project (across every cluster and region), or OMIT ALL THREE to list the organization's Ownkube Compute deployments (the managed, no-cluster deploy path — use this to see what you deployed with list_regions). Providing more than one is an error. Fourth step of the discovery spine.

environmentId.description: List every deployment in this environment.

clusterId.description: List every deployment on this cluster.

projectId.description: List every deployment in this project.

tools.name: create_deployment
tools.title: Create deployment
tools.description: Create a deployment. The body is a discriminated union on `resourceType` (`web`, `worker`, `job`, `database`, `function`), each carrying its own `config` block. Omit `clusterId` on a cluster-bound type to deploy onto Ownkube Compute. To build a web/worker/job from a repository, pass `github` ({owner, repo, branch}) and omit `config.repository`/`config.tag`; otherwise set both to the image to run. Pass `environmentId` (from list_environments) to pick the environment; omitted, the deployment goes into the project's default environment. Confirm with the user before calling.

environmentId.description: Environment to deploy into (an id from list_environments). If omitted, the deployment goes into the project's default environment.

repository.description: Image repository to run, e.g. nginx or ghcr.io/org/app. Omit when deploying from `github`; the image is built from the repository.

tag.description: Image tag to run. Omit when deploying from `github`.

requests.description: CPU and memory each replica is guaranteed. Settable only on your own cluster: on Ownkube Compute, Ownkube sets the requests and ignores any sent.

limits.description: CPU and memory each replica may use. On a metered Ownkube Compute app this is how you size it, up to the largest box; a reserved app, database or cache is sized by its box (skuId) instead.

resources.description: Per-replica CPU and memory. On Ownkube Compute, a metered app sets limits only (Ownkube sets the requests); a reserved app, database or cache is sized by its box, so change skuId to resize. Requests and limits are both settable only on your own cluster.

billingMode.description: Ownkube Compute only. metered (the default) bills measured CPU and memory; size it with resources.limits. reserved bills a flat box price per replica-hour and is sized by the box, so change skuId to resize. Ignored on your own cluster.

skuId.description: Box id for billingMode reserved (a Spark box, e.g. spark-4). Required with reserved, rejected otherwise. Change it to resize a reserved app.

environmentId.description: Environment to deploy into (an id from list_environments). If omitted, the deployment goes into the project's default environment.

repository.description: Image repository to run, e.g. nginx or ghcr.io/org/app. Omit when deploying from `github`; the image is built from the repository.

tag.description: Image tag to run. Omit when deploying from `github`.

billingMode.description: Ownkube Compute only, and always reserved: the database runs as a box (skuId) that sets its CPU and memory. Ignored on your own cluster.

skuId.description: Database box id from list_boxes (e.g. db-2). Required on Ownkube Compute; change it to resize the database.

tools.name: get_deployment
tools.title: Get deployment
tools.description: Fetch one deployment's full configuration by deploymentId (from list_deployments).

tools.name: delete_deployment
tools.title: Delete deployment
tools.description: Delete a deployment by id. This is irreversible. The workload and its data are torn down. Confirm with the user before calling.

tools.name: get_deployment_status
tools.title: Get deployment status
tools.description: Get the live rollout status (health, sync, phase) of one deployment by deploymentId (from list_deployments). When status is failed, statusMessage says why; a failed apply can be retried with resync_deployment.

tools.name: get_deployment_logs
tools.title: Get deployment logs
tools.description: Read recent application log lines for one deployment by deploymentId (from list_deployments).

rangeSeconds.description: How far back to read, in seconds (default 3600). Ignored when `start` and `end` are sent.

start.description: Window start, unix seconds. Send with `end` to read a fixed window instead of a look-back.

end.description: Window end, unix seconds, after `start`. Capped to now and to the plan's log retention.

limit.description: Max number of log lines to return (default 300).

filter.description: Regular expression matched against the log message; empty returns every line.

tools.name: list_functions
tools.title: List functions
tools.description: List the organization's Ownkube Compute functions. Functions are cluster-less (they attach to a cloud account + region, not a cluster) so they never appear in list_deployments scoped by clusterId — this is the dedicated function listing.

tools.name: get_function_source
tools.title: Get function source
tools.description: Read the stored inline source file for an Ownkube Compute function by deploymentId (from list_functions). Only valid for a Compute function; own-cloud functions and non-functions error. A freshly-created function whose upload hasn't landed yet returns not-found.

tools.name: get_connection_info
tools.title: Get connection info
tools.description: Get a database's or cache's full connection info by deploymentId: host, port, database name, username, password, and connection string (`uri`) for apps in the same environment, plus `publicUri` for connecting from outside when public access is on (`publicReady` says whether it accepts connections yet; `paused` means billing stopped it, data kept, and it accepts no connections until it resumes). The result contains live credentials: share them only with the user who asked. To wire an app to it, prefer link_datastore.

tools.name: link_datastore
tools.title: Link database or cache
tools.description: Connect an app (web, worker, or job) to a database or cache in the same environment: writes the connection string into the app's environment as a secret variable (DATABASE_URL, MONGODB_URI or REDIS_URL by default) and redeploys the app. The credential is never returned. An existing variable with the same name is replaced. Confirm with the user before calling.

datastoreId.description: The database or cache deployment id to link.

envVar.description: Environment variable to set. Defaults to DATABASE_URL for a database (MONGODB_URI for a MongoDB-compatible one) and REDIS_URL for a cache.

tools.name: update_deployment
tools.title: Update deployment
tools.description: Update a cluster-bound deployment (web/worker/job/database/cache) and record a revision. Send the config block matching the deployment's type: `appConfig` for web/worker, `jobConfig` for job, `databaseConfig` for database, `cacheConfig` for cache. When the deployment shows `imageSource: "managed"` (built by Ownkube), leave `repository` and `tag` out; the current build is kept. Use update_function for functions.

appConfig.description: New config for a web/worker deployment.

repository.description: Image repository to run, e.g. nginx or ghcr.io/org/app. Omit to keep the current image (always kept for an Ownkube build).

tag.description: Image tag to run. Omit to keep the current tag (always kept for an Ownkube build).

limits.description: CPU and memory each replica may use. On a metered Ownkube Compute app this is how you size it, up to the largest box; a reserved app, database or cache is sized by its box (skuId) instead.

resources.description: Per-replica CPU and memory. On Ownkube Compute, a metered app sets limits only (Ownkube sets the requests); a reserved app, database or cache is sized by its box, so change skuId to resize. Requests and limits are both settable only on your own cluster.

billingMode.description: Ownkube Compute only. metered (the default) bills measured CPU and memory; size it with resources.limits. reserved bills a flat box price per replica-hour and is sized by the box, so change skuId to resize. Ignored on your own cluster.

skuId.description: Box id for billingMode reserved (a Spark box, e.g. spark-4). Required with reserved, rejected otherwise. Change it to resize a reserved app.

databaseConfig.description: New config for a database deployment.

billingMode.description: Ownkube Compute only, and always reserved: the database runs as a box (skuId) that sets its CPU and memory. Ignored on your own cluster.

skuId.description: Database box id from list_boxes (e.g. db-2). Required on Ownkube Compute; change it to resize the database.

cacheConfig.description: New config for a cache deployment.

limits.description: CPU and memory each replica may use. On a metered Ownkube Compute app this is how you size it, up to the largest box; a reserved app, database or cache is sized by its box (skuId) instead.

resources.description: Per-replica CPU and memory. On Ownkube Compute, a metered app sets limits only (Ownkube sets the requests); a reserved app, database or cache is sized by its box, so change skuId to resize. Requests and limits are both settable only on your own cluster.

jobConfig.description: New config for a job deployment.

repository.description: Image repository to run, e.g. nginx or ghcr.io/org/app. Omit to keep the current image (always kept for an Ownkube build).

tag.description: Image tag to run. Omit to keep the current tag (always kept for an Ownkube build).

requests.description: CPU and memory each replica is guaranteed. Settable only on your own cluster: on Ownkube Compute, Ownkube sets the requests and ignores any sent.

limits.description: CPU and memory each replica may use. On a metered Ownkube Compute app this is how you size it, up to the largest box; a reserved app, database or cache is sized by its box (skuId) instead.

resources.description: Per-replica CPU and memory. On Ownkube Compute, a metered app sets limits only (Ownkube sets the requests); a reserved app, database or cache is sized by its box, so change skuId to resize. Requests and limits are both settable only on your own cluster.

sendSsoInvites.description: Email a sign-on invite to newly added allow-list addresses.

tools.name: update_function
tools.title: Update function
tools.description: Update a `function`-type deployment's config (handler, runtime, env, triggers) and record a revision.

tools.name: deploy_function
tools.title: Deploy function
tools.description: Ship a new revision of an Ownkube Compute function: apply the config knobs (env, timeout, triggers) and, when `code` is given, upload the new inline source — folding both into one revision. Omit `code` to change settings only. Not valid for own-cloud functions (use update_function).

code.description: New inline source. Omit to change settings only.

filename.description: Source filename (defaults to the current entrypoint).

tools.name: copy_deployment
tools.title: Copy deployment
tools.description: Clone a deployment's current config into another environment, creating a new deployment. Not valid for functions.

copy.description: The target environment/cluster for the copy.

tools.name: list_job_runs
tools.title: List job runs
tools.description: List a scheduled job deployment's recent runs. Non-job deployments return an empty, non-existent history rather than erroring.

tools.name: trigger_job_run
tools.title: Trigger job run
tools.description: Trigger an immediate run of a scheduled job deployment.

tools.name: cancel_job_run
tools.title: Cancel job run
tools.description: Cancel an in-flight run of a scheduled job deployment (terminates its pods). The named run must belong to this deployment.

tools.name: restart_deployment
tools.title: Restart deployment
tools.description: Rollout-restart a running web or worker deployment (replaces every pod with the same image). Not a rebuild and not a new revision. Only valid for web/worker deployments that are already live.

tools.name: resync_deployment
tools.title: Resync deployment
tools.description: Re-apply a deployment's current settings to its cluster with no config change and no new revision. Use it when get_deployment_status shows a failed or stalled rollout, including for databases and caches (restart_deployment is web/worker only). Not valid for functions.

tools.name: set_auto_deploy
tools.title: Set auto-deploy
tools.description: Turn auto-deploy on or off for a source-backed deployment. Reuses the branch captured at create time. Rejected for deployments without a source repository.

tools.name: set_maintenance_mode
tools.title: Set maintenance mode
tools.description: Divert a public web deployment's URL to a branded maintenance page (the workload keeps running). Only valid once public access is on and the first build has completed.

enabled.description: Whether maintenance mode should be on.

message.description: Optional line shown on the maintenance page. Ignored when disabling.

tools.name: rename_deployment
tools.title: Rename deployment
tools.description: Set (or clear) a deployment's cosmetic display label. Never touches the immutable name / cluster identity, cuts no revision, and does not re-sync. Empty/whitespace clears it.

displayName.description: Cosmetic display label. Empty/whitespace clears it (falls back to the immutable name).

tools.name: move_deployment_to_project
tools.title: Move deployment to project
tools.description: Re-file a deployment under a different project (from list_projects). A project is a purely organizational grouping, so this is a control-plane-only change: it cuts no revision, doesn't re-sync the cluster, and keeps the environment, address, and running workloads exactly where they are. A marketplace app and its managed database/cache move together as one group.

targetProjectId.description: The project to re-file this deployment under.

tools.name: set_build_args
tools.title: Set build arguments
tools.description: Replace the custom build-time arguments for a deployment that builds on your cluster. Applies on the next build. An empty map clears them.

buildArgs.description: Build arguments as a key/value map.

tools.name: set_build_context
tools.title: Set build root directory
tools.description: Set the root directory (build context) for a deployment that builds on your cluster — how a monorepo app in a subdirectory gets built. Applies on the next build. Empty string clears it.

contextPath.description: Root directory for the build, relative to the repo root. Empty string clears it.

tools.name: set_builder_size
tools.title: Set builder size
tools.description: Set the build pod's size (small / standard / large) for a deployment that builds on your cluster. Applies on the next build. On Ownkube Compute, `large` requires the Team plan.

tools.name: check_subdomain
tools.title: Check address availability
tools.description: Check whether an address label is legal and free right now for this deployment. `current: true` means it's the label the deployment already holds.

tools.name: suggest_subdomains
tools.title: Suggest available addresses
tools.description: Return a handful of address labels that are free right now, seeded from the deployment name (or the `desired` seed) and namespaced with the environment and organization when they read well.

desired.description: Seed the suggestions from what the user has typed so far.

limit.description: How many suggestions to return (1 to 12).

tools.name: change_subdomain
tools.title: Change public address
tools.description: Move a public web app to a chosen address label and re-sync its route. The old address stops resolving. Not valid for databases. Confirm with the user before calling.

subdomain.description: The new address label to claim.

tools.name: list_vcs_connections
tools.title: List connected repository accounts
tools.description: List the GitHub and GitLab accounts connected to the organization. When none is connected, send the user to `connectUrl` to connect one; that step is dashboard-only.

tools.name: list_vcs_repositories
tools.title: List repositories
tools.description: List repositories the organization's connected GitHub and GitLab accounts can see. A repository missing here needs access granted in the dashboard (see list_vcs_connections).

connectionId.description: Only list this connected account's repositories. Omit to list across every connected account.

tools.name: list_vcs_branches
tools.title: List repository branches
tools.description: List a connected repository's branches, most recently committed first. Use it to pick the branch for set_deployment_source.

connectionId.description: Connected account to read through. Omit to use whichever connected account can see the repository.

tools.name: set_deployment_source
tools.title: Connect a repository to an app
tools.description: Connect a repository and branch to an existing app (or switch them) and deploy it. Settings, secrets, linked databases, address and resources are kept, and pushes to the branch then deploy automatically. The repository must be visible to a connected account (list_vcs_repositories).

repository.description: Repository as owner/repo (GitLab: group/subgroup/project). A trailing .git is fine.

branch.description: Branch to deploy and track; pushes to it deploy automatically.

connectionId.description: Connected account to use (from list_vcs_connections). Omit to use whichever connected account can see the repository.

contextPath.description: Root directory to build from, relative to the repository root. Empty string means the repository root.

dockerfilePath.description: Dockerfile path relative to the root directory. Empty string means the default Dockerfile.

watchPaths.description: Globs such as src/** or !docs/**: a push deploys only when a changed file matches. An empty list deploys on every push.

waitForChecks.description: Hold push deploys until the commit's CI checks pass; a failing check skips the deploy.

deploy.description: Build and deploy now (default true). false saves the source and waits for the next push or rebuild.

commit.description: Deploy this commit SHA instead of the branch tip. The branch is still tracked for later pushes.

tools.name: clear_deployment_source
tools.title: Disconnect an app's repository
tools.description: Disconnect the app's repository so pushes stop deploying; it then redeploys only from uploaded source. The running version keeps serving and nothing is rebuilt.

tools.name: list_variables
tools.title: List app variables
tools.description: List a web app's, worker's or job's effective variables by deploymentId: the environment's shared ones plus the app's own, each with its `source` and whether it overrides a shared value. Secret values are always empty; their names are listed.

deploymentId.description: The app (web, worker or job) whose variables to use.

tools.name: set_variables
tools.title: Set app variables
tools.description: Add, change or remove a web app's, worker's or job's own variables in one save (`set` and `unset`), rolled out as one redeploy. Untouched variables, secrets included, keep their values; `secret: true` stores a value write-only. Variables shared by the environment are changed with update_environment instead. Confirm with the user before calling.

deploymentId.description: The app (web, worker or job) whose variables to use.

set.description: Variables to add or change on this app. A name shared by the environment is overridden for this app only.

name.description: Variable name: letters, numbers and underscores, not starting with a number.

value.description: The new value. A secret can't be empty; to drop a variable, list its name under `unset` instead.

secret.description: Store as a secret (never returned on reads). Omit to keep the variable's current flag; a new variable defaults to plain.

unset.description: Names to remove from this app. Only the app's own variables can be removed; shared ones are changed on the environment.

tools.name: list_revisions
tools.title: List revisions
tools.description: List the revision history of a deployment by id, newest first. Each revision carries canRollback: only the most recent builds can be rolled back to.

tools.name: rollback_deployment
tools.title: Roll back deployment
tools.description: Restore an earlier revision's config onto a deployment and record a new revision. Only recent builds can be rolled back to (see canRollback in list_revisions); older ones are rejected. Confirm with the user before calling.

revisionId.description: The revision id to roll back to.

note.description: Optional note recorded on the rollback.

tools.name: promote_deployment
tools.title: Promote deployment
tools.description: Copy one deployment's current config onto another (e.g. staging → production), recording a revision on the target and linking it back to the source. The two deployments must differ.

note.description: Optional note recorded on the promotion.

tools.name: rebuild_deployment
tools.title: Rebuild deployment from source
tools.description: Rebuild an in-cluster deployment from the current head of its tracked branch, or from a specific commit when one is given — the manual counterpart to the push trigger. Queues a build and supersedes any in-flight one. Only valid for deployments that build from source.

note.description: Optional note recorded on the queued revision.

commit.description: Commit sha (7 to 40 hex characters) to build instead of the tracked branch's current head.

tools.name: create_source_upload
tools.title: Create source upload
tools.description: Get a one-time upload URL for an app's source code: step 1 of deploying local code that has no connected repository. Package the project as a gzipped tarball with its files at the archive root, leaving out dependencies, build output and .git, e.g. `tar -czf /tmp/source.tar.gz --exclude=node_modules --exclude=.git -C <project dir> .`. Then upload it: `curl -X PUT -H "Content-Type: application/gzip" --data-binary @/tmp/source.tar.gz "<uploadUrl>"`. The tarball must be at most maxBytes and the URL expires at expiresAt (15 minutes). Then call deploy_uploaded_source with the uploadId. Pass deploymentId when the upload will redeploy an existing app. Fails up front, with a link to add credit, when the wallet is empty.

deploymentId.description: The app this upload will redeploy. Omit when the upload will create a new app.

tools.name: deploy_uploaded_source
tools.title: Deploy uploaded source
tools.description: Build and deploy source uploaded with create_source_upload: step 2 of deploying local code. Without deploymentId it creates a new app on Ownkube Compute and picks defaults for anything omitted: a name from nameHint (pass the project's directory name; made unique), the region the organization already uses (else the default), the port from the Dockerfile's EXPOSE or the detected framework (else 8080), a public URL for web apps, and the default project and environment. The defaults block in the result says what was chosen; tell the user. With deploymentId it rebuilds that existing app from the new upload instead. Follow the build with get_build_logs (revisionId) and get_deployment_status. Confirm with the user before calling.

name.description: Exact deployment name. Fails if taken. Omit to derive one from nameHint.

nameHint.description: Free-form name source (e.g. the project's directory name). Slugified and suffixed (-2, -3, …) if taken. Defaults to "app".

region.description: Region slug from list_regions. Defaults to the region the organization already deploys in, else the platform default.

port.description: Port the app listens on (also passed as PORT). Defaults to the Dockerfile's EXPOSE, else the detected framework's default, else 8080.

resourceType.description: web (default, serves HTTP) or worker (background process).

public.description: Give a web app a public URL. Defaults to true for web.

projectId.description: Project id from list_projects. Defaults to the organization's default project.

environmentId.description: Environment id from list_environments. Defaults to the project's default environment.

note.description: Optional note recorded on the build.

deploymentId.description: Redeploy this existing app from the upload. Omit to create a new app; the create-only fields below are rejected when it's set.

tools.name: get_deployment_telemetry
tools.title: Get deployment telemetry
tools.description: Read the overview telemetry tiles — CPU, memory, request rate, p95 latency, and network in/out — for one deployment over the requested window. `network` is pod network traffic in and out (bytes/sec rate plus a window total in bytes); it counts all traffic, including traffic between your services, so it reads higher than billed bandwidth (data sent to the internet only). `network` is null for Compute functions. A capacity of 0 means no fixed ceiling is set (usage can burst). Returns null when the cluster isn't reachable yet.

rangeSeconds.description: How far back to read, in seconds (default 3600).

tools.name: get_deployment_observability
tools.title: Get deployment observability
tools.description: Read the expanded observability series — per-status-class request rate, latency percentiles, CPU/memory time-series, and network in/out series — for one deployment. `network` is pod network traffic in and out (bytes/sec rate plus a window total in bytes); it counts all traffic, including traffic between your services, so it reads higher than billed bandwidth (data sent to the internet only). `network` is null for Compute functions. `hasRequestData` is false for workloads whose gateway doesn't report per-deployment request telemetry. Returns null when the cluster isn't reachable yet.

rangeSeconds.description: How far back to read, in seconds (default 3600).

tools.name: get_database_telemetry
tools.title: Get database telemetry
tools.description: Read database-shaped telemetry — connections, disk usage, database size, CPU, memory, transaction rate, and network in/out. `network` is pod network traffic in and out (bytes/sec rate plus a window total in bytes); it counts all traffic, including traffic between your services, so it reads higher than billed bandwidth (data sent to the internet only). A capacity of 0 means no fixed ceiling is set. Returns null for non-database deployments or when the cluster isn't reachable yet.

rangeSeconds.description: How far back to read, in seconds (default 3600).

tools.name: get_cache_telemetry
tools.title: Get cache telemetry
tools.description: Read cache-shaped telemetry — connected clients, memory, ops/sec, hit rate, CPU, disk, and network in/out. `network` is pod network traffic in and out (bytes/sec rate plus a window total in bytes); it counts all traffic, including traffic between your services, so it reads higher than billed bandwidth (data sent to the internet only). A capacity of 0 means no fixed ceiling is set. Returns null for non-cache deployments or when the cluster isn't reachable yet.

rangeSeconds.description: How far back to read, in seconds (default 3600).

tools.name: get_function_telemetry
tools.title: Get function telemetry
tools.description: Read invocation-shaped telemetry — invocations, errors, duration, throttles, and concurrency — for a function deployment. Returns null for non-function deployments or when the function isn't provisioned yet.

rangeSeconds.description: How far back to read, in seconds (default 3600).

tools.name: get_build_logs
tools.title: Get build logs
tools.description: Read the build output for one revision (from list_revisions) — the live build while it runs, else the durable store once it settles. Best-effort: returns an empty log when no build output is available.

revisionId.description: The revision id whose build to read.

tailLines.description: Number of trailing log lines to return (default 2000).

tools.name: list_alert_rules
tools.title: List alert rules
tools.description: List the workload alert rules configured on one Ownkube Compute deployment (newest first).

tools.name: create_alert_rule
tools.title: Create alert rule
tools.description: Create a metric alert rule on an Ownkube Compute deployment. For cpu/memory the threshold is a percent of the app's limit (≤ 100); for restarts it's a raw count. Only valid for Ownkube Compute deployments.

metric.description: cpu/memory compare a percent of the app's limit; restarts is a raw count.

comparator.description: Fire when the value is greater-than (gt) or less-than (lt).

forDurationSeconds.description: How long the condition must hold before firing (default 300).

tools.name: update_alert_rule
tools.title: Update alert rule
tools.description: Edit an alert rule's fields or toggle it on/off. All fields except ruleId are optional; percent metrics still cap the threshold at 100.

metric.description: cpu/memory compare a percent of the app's limit; restarts is a raw count.

comparator.description: Fire when the value is greater-than (gt) or less-than (lt).

forDurationSeconds.description: How long the condition must hold before firing (default 300).

enabled.description: Turn the rule on or off without deleting it.

tools.name: delete_alert_rule
tools.title: Delete alert rule
tools.description: Permanently delete one alert rule from a deployment. Get the rule id from list_alert_rules. The rule stops firing at once and can't be restored; its past firings stay in list_alert_firings. To pause a rule instead, set enabled to false with update_alert_rule.

tools.name: list_alert_firings
tools.title: List alert firings
tools.description: List recent alert firings for the organization, optionally scoped to one deployment. A firing is recorded when a rule starts breaching and marked resolved when it recovers.

deploymentId.description: Scope to one deployment (omit for the whole org).

limit.description: Max number of firings to return (default 50).

tools.name: list_custom_domains
tools.title: List custom domains
tools.description: List the custom domains linked to one web app. On Ownkube Compute it also returns the plan's custom-domain allowance; on a Starter cluster, the parent domains connected on the cluster. Each linked host carries the DNS records the customer sets.

tools.name: link_custom_domain
tools.title: Link custom domain
tools.description: Link a host (a subdomain like `app.customer.com`, or the apex `customer.com`) to a public web app. On Ownkube Compute any host can be linked directly and each counts toward the plan's custom-domain allowance; on a Starter cluster the parent domain must already be connected on the cluster (list_custom_domains shows them). Returns the linked host with the DNS records to create.

hostname.description: The host to link — a subdomain or the apex of a parent.

tools.name: verify_custom_domain
tools.title: Recheck custom domain
tools.description: Re-run the reconcile for a linked host and report its certificate status. The host goes live once its routing record resolves and the certificate is active.

tools.name: unlink_custom_domain
tools.title: Unlink custom domain
tools.description: Detach a host from its deployment. On Ownkube Compute its certificate is removed too; on a Starter cluster the parent domain stays connected for other apps.

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.title: Send feedback to the Ownkube team
tools.description:
Send feedback to the Ownkube team about anything you tried to do here: a tool call that failed, something the user asked for that these tools can't do, a result that looked wrong, an error or description that confused you, missing docs, or an idea. Reports are read by the people who build these tools and decide what gets fixed next, so a specific report from you is worth more than a vague one from anyone.

When to call it:
- A tool returned an error you couldn't resolve, or a task stayed stuck (deploy, build, status) past a reasonable wait. category: failed.
- The user asked for something no tool, input, or option supports, and you had to stop or send them to the dashboard. category: missing_capability.
- A call succeeded but the result was wrong or contradicted another read (status healthy while the app is down, a setting that didn't stick). category: bug.
- You had to guess what a tool, input, or error meant, or picked the wrong tool first because of its description. category: confusing.
- Instructions or docs were missing or wrong. category: docs_gap.
- You see a better way for a tool or flow to work. category: suggestion. Something that went notably well: worked_well.

How to call it:
- Finish or stop the user's task first; send one report per distinct problem, at the point you know the outcome. Don't send duplicates, and don't report every routine retry that then worked.
- You don't need the user's permission: it changes nothing in their account. Mention in your reply that you sent it, with the reference.
- summary: one line naming the tool and the problem. goal: what the user wanted. attempted: tools called in order with the inputs that mattered. outcome: the exact error text and code, or the values you saw. expected: what would have let you finish. workaround: what you did instead. tools and resourceIds: names and ids involved. client: your client and model. severity: blocker, degraded, or minor.
- Never include passwords, tokens, API keys, connection strings, environment variable values, or the user's private data. Describe them ("the database connection string") instead. Obvious secrets are redacted on receipt, but don't rely on it.
- This is not a support channel: nobody replies here. For billing, account, or urgent production issues, point the user to the Ownkube dashboard.

category.description: What kind of report this is. failed: a tool call or task did not complete (error, timeout, stuck status). missing_capability: what the user asked for has no tool, input, or option here. bug: something completed but the result is wrong or inconsistent (status says healthy but the app is down, a value didn't stick). confusing: a tool name, description, input, error, or output misled you or made you guess. docs_gap: instructions or docs were missing, wrong, or out of date. suggestion: an improvement idea. worked_well: something that went smoothly and should stay that way.

severity.description: Impact on the user's task. blocker: the task could not be finished. degraded: finished only partly, or with a workaround. minor: an annoyance that did not change the result. Omit for suggestion and worked_well.

summary.description: One line a person can triage without reading the rest, e.g. 'create_deployment rejects a Dockerfile in a subfolder with no hint about set_build_context'.

goal.description: What the user asked for, or what you were trying to accomplish, in plain words. Paraphrase; don't paste the whole conversation.

attempted.description: The steps you took, in order: which tools you called, with the inputs that mattered, and anything else you tried (retries, alternatives). Never include passwords, tokens, keys, or connection strings.

outcome.description: What actually happened: the exact error message and code, the status or field values you saw, how long you waited. Quote errors verbatim (with secrets removed); they are the most useful part of a report.

expected.description: What you expected instead, or what would have let you finish (a tool, an input, a clearer error, a doc).

workaround.description: How you got around it, if you did, or what you told the user to do by hand (for example, use the dashboard).

tools.description: Names of the tools involved, most relevant first, e.g. ['create_deployment', 'get_build_logs'].

resourceIds.description: Ids of the deployments, clusters, projects, environments, or revisions involved, so the team can look at the exact resource.

client.description: Your client and model, e.g. 'Claude Code, claude-opus-5-5', so reports can be grouped by agent.
